# Dynamic Island + `⌘P` — Implementation Specification > Implementation companion to `OCEAN_DESKTOP_NORTH_STAR.md`. > > Scope: define the smallest complete first build of Ocean Desktop's Dynamic > Island and its keyboard-first session focus/search mode. This is deliberately > concrete: data contracts, components, files, state transitions, keyboard > routing, CSS geometry, acceptance checks, and explicitly deferred work. > > The practical delivery sequence and commit gates live in > [`OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BUILD_PLAN.md`](OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BUILD_PLAN.md). ## Decision summary Build this before a permanent left rail. The first release is **not** a generalized desktop task system. It is a Tauri-only, titlebar-adjacent focus surface backed by the existing daemon session catalogue. ### V1 ships - compact Dynamic Island in the desktop header - focused session identity plus a count of active-background sessions - click to open an Island overlay - overlay lists active/recent sessions with project/path/branch/origin metadata - selecting a result calls the existing `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` and moves that session into the center transcript - `⌘P` opens that same overlay in search mode - fuzzy search over existing session metadata - arrow keys, Enter, Escape, click-outside behavior ### V1 does not ship - inline reply to a background session - cross-session live streaming in the Island - server-side/session-content semantic search - approvals, CI, GitHub, browser, rooms, Council, files, or PR results - a left rail - a replacement for the existing web/extension Sessions modal Those are follow-on waves after the core focus interaction is proven. ## Existing foundations to reuse Do not recreate these systems: | Existing implementation | Reuse in Island work | | --- | --- | | `Daemon::sessions: RwSignal>` | search corpus and list data | | `Daemon::session_id: RwSignal>` | focused-session identity | | `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` | sole session focus/switch operation | | `sessions.rs::split_origin`, `fmt_relative_time`, `session_root`, project lookup | display metadata and normalized search text | | `palette.rs::fuzzy_score` behavior | fuzzy scoring semantics; extract/move to a shared search helper rather than copy it | | `PaletteView` keyboard pattern | input autofocus, ArrowUp/Down, Enter, Escape, backdrop click | | `app.rs` `window_event_listener(ev::keydown, ...)` | `⌘P` global shortcut and overlay Escape priority | | `host::running_in_tauri()` | mount/gating boundary | | `styles/chrome.css` titlebar model | titlebar position and drag-region rules | Important fact: today `Daemon::switch_session` replaces the active transcript and reconnects its SSE/permission streams. The Island must call it; it must not attempt a second transcript/session runtime of its own. ## User-facing model ### Terminology - **Focused session**: the daemon's current `session_id`; it owns the center transcript and composer. - **Background session**: any other persisted session in the catalogue. V1 treats "recent" as the only reliable activity signal. - **Island**: compact titlebar control plus its expanded overlay. - **Search mode**: overlay opened by `⌘P`, with input focused. - **Browse mode**: overlay opened by click, with input present but not focused or visually secondary. Do not call every session "active" in V1. The client currently observes an SSE stream only for the focused session, so it cannot truthfully determine whether other sessions are presently generating work. Use **recent sessions** until the daemon publishes cross-session activity. ### V1 interaction flow ```text Focused center session: A Catalogue: A, B, C, D header Island (closed) [ A · Ocean Surface · 3 recent ] click Island OR press ⌘P → Island overlay opens → list shows A, B, C, D ordered by focus/recentness choose B + Enter/click → Daemon::switch_session(B.id, B.title) → B becomes focused center session → overlay closes → A remains in the catalogue and appears in future Island results ``` No extra "slotting" persistence is needed for V1. The natural catalogue order already makes the old focused session available. Explicit pins/orbits can arrive later only if observed usage requires them. ## Data model Create a new `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs` module. ### Core types ```rust #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum IslandMode { Closed, Browse, Search, } #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub enum IslandPriority { Focused, Recent, Background, } #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct IslandSession { pub id: String, pub title: String, pub project: Option, pub cwd: String, pub branch: Option, pub origin: Option, pub updated_at: String, pub turn_count: u32, pub is_focused: bool, pub priority: IslandPriority, } #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub enum IslandResult { Session(IslandSession), } ``` Keep V1's result enum even though it has one variant. It establishes the extension seam for `Approval`, `BrowserTask`, `CiRun`, `File`, and `GitHubPull` without forcing speculative implementations today. ### Derivation function Expose a pure function in `island.rs`: ```rust pub(crate) fn derive_island_sessions( sessions: &[SessionSummary], projects: &[ProjectInfo], focused_id: Option<&str>, ) -> Vec; ``` Rules: 1. Retain every daemon-catalogued session, including zero-turn drafts. This follows `sessions.rs::group_for_panel` parity. 2. Resolve project display name via `owning_project`, then `project_for_root`. 3. Parse `[WEB]`, `[?]`, etc. title prefix using a reusable public helper from `sessions.rs` or a new shared metadata module. Do not duplicate parsing. 4. Sort: - focused session first, - then `updated_at` newest-first, - stable tie-breaker by title/id. 5. `priority` is `Focused` for focused session; `Recent` for sessions updated in the existing `is_recent` window; `Background` otherwise. 6. No claims about remote/live activity in V1. ### Search document and scoring Create a testable pure helper: ```rust pub(crate) fn island_search_text(item: &IslandSession) -> String; pub(crate) fn search_island( query: &str, items: &[IslandSession], ) -> Vec; ``` Search text joins, lowercased, with separators: ```text title project cwd branch origin state turns ``` Examples that must work: ```text north star project:ocean-surface // V1 literal text match is enough; facets deferred src/app.rs main tauri recent ``` Scoring: - empty query: existing derivation order - exact/prefix match in title: strongest boost - project match: second boost - cwd/branch/origin: normal fuzzy score - focused item: tie-break boost, not enough to hide better matches - recency: tie-break boost Extract `palette.rs::fuzzy_score` and the word-boundary helper into either: - `src/search.rs` (recommended), or - `pub(crate)` helpers in `palette.rs` Use the same scorer rather than making `⌘P` feel inconsistent with `⌘K`. ## Component API and ownership ### `Island` component ```rust #[component] pub fn Island( daemon: Daemon, mode: RwSignal, ) -> impl IntoView ``` `app.rs` owns `mode`, because it coordinates: - header click - `⌘P` - global Escape ordering - any future deep links / menu actions `Island` owns local overlay state: ```rust let query = RwSignal::new(String::new()); let selected_index = RwSignal::new(0usize); let input_ref = NodeRef::::new(); ``` ### Required component DOM shape ```text section.island-host // mounted inside .ocean-header button.island-chip // compact/default state focused session identity background/recent count state dot Show(mode != Closed) div.island-scrim // full window click target, below header section.island-popover // anchored below chip form / div island-search input.island-search__input div.island-results div.island-group button.island-result ``` Important: render `island-host` inside the header so the chip naturally occupies the titlebar zone. Render the scrim/popover with `position: fixed` and a high z-index so it is not clipped by the header and so its click-outside behavior is reliable. ### Compact chip behavior When no focused session exists: ```text Ocean · no session [open] ``` When focused session exists: ```text {title} · {project?} · {recent_count} recent ``` Constraints: - max compact width `520px` on wide desktop headers; responsive percentage and narrow-window caps must preserve both titlebar control zones - title line truncates - project is optional and truncates before title is hidden - no persistent animation unless attention becomes real in later slices - click toggles Browse; if Search is open, click closes - chip itself must not carry `data-tauri-drag-region` because it is interactive ### Overlay behavior - browse result limit: 8 initial rows (scroll beyond) - search result limit: 20 initial rows - result rows show: - title - project/path, branch, origin, relative time, turns - focused marker when applicable - click result: switch and close - no inline reply in V1 - background/scrim click: close ### Search-mode focus effect In `Island`, add an effect equivalent to `PaletteView`: ```rust Effect::new(move |_| { if mode.get() == IslandMode::Search { request_animation_frame(move || { if let Some(input) = input_ref.get() { let _ = input.focus(); input.select(); } }); } }); ``` Use the repo's existing rAF/focus utility if available; do not invent a setTimeout-based race. ## `app.rs` changes ### Imports and modules 1. Add `mod island;` in the crate root (`lib.rs` / module declaration location used by the project). 2. Import `Island`, `IslandMode` in `app.rs`. ### State Near `workspace_open` setup: ```rust let island_mode: RwSignal = RwSignal::new(IslandMode::Closed); let daemon_for_island = StoredValue::new(daemon.clone()); ``` No localStorage persistence in V1. An open overlay should not survive restart. ### Header mount Replace the Tauri interpretation of the current Sessions header trigger. Current code at `app.rs` roughly lines 958–971 renders a permanent labeled `Sessions` button. Change the header layout to: ```rust
...
... existing runtime + overflow + workspace controls ...
``` Do **not** move runtime status into the Island in V1. It already has stable presentation and should remain where it is. ### Shortcut routing Add a new focused listener before/alongside the current Escape listener: ```rust let _island_shortcut = window_event_listener(ev::keydown, move |e| { let is_cmd_p = (e.meta_key() || e.ctrl_key()) && !e.shift_key() && !e.alt_key() && e.key().eq_ignore_ascii_case("p"); if is_cmd_p && in_tauri { e.prevent_default(); e.stop_propagation(); island_mode.set(IslandMode::Search); } }); on_cleanup(move || _island_shortcut.remove()); ``` Use both Meta and Ctrl so the browser/PWA can share the behavior later if wanted, but gate initial mounting/handling on `in_tauri` to prevent intercepting browser print on non-Tauri hosts. ### Escape priority Update the existing global Escape ladder: ```text 1. PaletteView / Island local input handlers stop propagation themselves. 2. Council stage 3. Island overlay 4. Rooms 5. Sessions modal 6. Deck ``` The Island component's own input handler must call `stop_propagation()` on Escape after closing itself. The global handler only catches unhandled Escape from click/browse state. ### Sessions command Keep `toggle-sessions` unchanged in V1. It remains the deep browse fallback. Add a new command registry entry: ```rust Command { id: "focus-search", title: "Search Ocean…".into(), hint: Some("⌘P".into()), scope: CommandScope::App, slash: None, enabled: Signal::derive(move || in_tauri), run: Callback::new(move |_| island_mode.set(IslandMode::Search)), } ``` This makes the action discoverable in `⌘K` and native menubar work later while preserving the semantic separation: `⌘K` invokes the search surface; `⌘P` is the direct shortcut. ### No transcript/composer changes in V1 Do not remove the Sessions landing action or alter the composer in the Island first slice. The Island must prove useful before changing existing navigation fallbacks. ## Keyboard specification | Key | When Island input is focused | Behavior | | --- | --- | --- | | `⌘P` / `Ctrl+P` | anywhere in Tauri app | open/replace with Search mode; focus/select input | | `Esc` | search/browse overlay | close Island; prevent bubble | | `ArrowDown` | results non-empty | next result, wrapping | | `ArrowUp` | results non-empty | previous result, wrapping | | `Enter` | result selected | `switch_session`; close Island | | `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | search/browse overlay | keep focus in the combobox; results use `aria-activedescendant` | | click chip | closed | open Browse | | click chip | open | close | | click scrim | open | close | | click row | open | `switch_session`; close | Do not bind `⌘P` within a textarea only. It must work while transcript, composer, workspace, or header controls have focus. Respect IME composition if the app already exposes an equivalent guard; otherwise add it before intercepting the shortcut. ## CSS implementation Create `styles/island.css`; add it to `index.html` after `chrome.css` and before `panels.css`. Also add it to any explicit extension-style copy/build list only if the build requires every stylesheet to exist there. The component does not mount off-Tauri, so it remains visually inert on web/extension. ### Geometry tokens ```css :root { --island-max-w: 360px; --island-popover-w: min(560px, calc(100vw - 32px)); --island-top: 64px; /* header bottom + seam; revise against live Tauri shot */ } ``` ### Required layering ```text workspace pane 50 web deck 60 modal sessions 100 Island scrim/popover 120 command palette 1100 ``` The Island must sit above the workspace and ordinary panels, below `⌘K` palette. This means opening `⌘K` visually wins even if Island search is open; opening the palette should close Island as a small follow-up hardening task. ### Styling constraints - Island chip uses the existing OCEAN depth ramp, not iOS visual imitation. - No giant pill and no floating dashboard card. - Use a compact rounded capsule only because it communicates one living, titlebar-adjacent object. - Popover is a single elevated material surface with a crisp border; result rows use tone changes, not individually elevated cards. - Header must remain draggable around the Island. Keep left/right noninteractive zones as `data-tauri-drag-region`; explicitly omit it on chip, input, and rows. - At `< 840px` desktop width, reduce chip metadata to title + count. At widths too narrow for a usable popover, allow the fixed overlay to span the safe viewport width; do not introduce a different mobile design in this slice. ### Initial selectors ```css .ocean-header { position: relative; } .island-host { position: absolute; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); } .island-chip { /* compact titlebar control */ } .island-scrim { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 120; } .island-popover { position: fixed; z-index: 121; top: var(--island-top); left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); } .island-search__input { /* palette-like focus treatment */ } .island-result { /* one full-width interactive row */ } .island-result--selected { /* selected keyboard row */ } .island-result--focused { /* understated current-session marker */ } ``` Do not use `overflow: hidden` on `.ocean-header`; it would clip the popover. ## File-by-file change list | Path | Change | | --- | --- | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/lib.rs` or current module root | declare `mod island;` | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs` | new pure derivation/search helpers + `Island` component + tests | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/app.rs` | Island state, header mount, `⌘P`, Escape priority, registry command | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/sessions.rs` | expose/shared metadata helpers only if needed; do not move panel UI | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/palette.rs` | move fuzzy scorer to a shared module or expose it safely; no duplicated score algorithm | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/search.rs` | recommended new shared fuzzy scorer if extraction is clean | | `styles/island.css` | new Island geometry and skin | | `index.html` | add stylesheet link | | extension build/style wiring | only if stylesheet packaging explicitly requires it | | `docs/OCEAN_DESKTOP_NORTH_STAR.md` | already records product direction; add implementation-doc link if docs use a links section | ## Tests ### Unit tests in `island.rs` - focused session sorts first - newer background sessions sort before older sessions - project derives from `owning_project` - project falls back to workspace-root match - origin prefix is stripped from title and exposed separately - title query beats project/path-only fuzzy query - empty query preserves derived order - `recent` / state text appears in searchable text if the chosen V1 behavior supports literal state queries - zero-turn session remains searchable ### Existing regression checks - `sessions.rs` grouping tests remain unchanged and pass - `palette.rs` fuzzy tests pass after helper extraction - verify `Daemon::switch_session` remains the only focus switch path ### Manual desktop acceptance run 1. Start Tauri app with ≥4 persisted sessions across ≥2 projects. 2. Verify chip is centered and does not overlap traffic lights, runtime controls, or workspace toggle. 3. Click chip: browse overlay opens, shows focused session first. 4. Click outside: closes. 5. Press `⌘P` from composer, workspace, and header: search opens and input has focus each time. 6. Type project, branch, title, cwd, and origin queries; confirm expected result. 7. Arrow down/up/Enter switches session and overlay closes. 8. Confirm old session is available when opening Island again. 9. Confirm `⌘K` palette still works and Escape closes exactly the topmost open surface. 10. Resize Tauri to narrow and wide widths; verify usable overlay geometry. 11. Verify browser PWA and extension preserve their existing Sessions-modal and browser-print behavior. ## Build sequence / commits Do not put all behavior in one giant commit. ### Commit 1 — Pure Island index - new `island.rs` types/derivation/search helpers - extract shared fuzzy score - unit tests only - no UI **Exit:** `cargo test` for the UI crate passes. ### Commit 2 — Island visual shell - component mounts on Tauri header - closed/browse state - display derived session rows - click row switches session - CSS and stylesheet wiring **Exit:** click-only interaction works; web has no visual change. ### Commit 3 — `⌘P` search mode - global shortcut - search input/focus - filtering, selection, keyboard navigation - Escape priority - registry discoverability command **Exit:** keyboard-only session focus switching works. ### Commit 4 — Live desktop polish - inspect an actual Tauri screenshot - tune titlebar spacing, type scale, row density, result limit, focus ring - run narrow/wide regressions **Exit:** the control feels built into the native shell rather than pasted over web chrome. ## Follow-up contract: required daemon work before richer Island states Do not fake background activity with only timestamps. For V2+ Island items, request an explicit daemon-owned stream/snapshot that can represent cross-session work truth: ```rust struct WorkAttentionItem { id: String, kind: Session | Permission | Browser | Ci | GitHub | Room | Council, session_id: Option, title: String, detail: Option, state: Idle | Running | NeedsHuman | Failed | Complete, updated_at: String, priority: u8, } ``` The daemon should own the source of truth. The Island is a reducer/view of that stream. This preserves the existing many-surfaces-one-daemon architecture and prevents a Tauri-only notion of work state. ## Explicit non-goal guardrails - Do not build inline quick reply until the daemon supports a safe background session prompt lifecycle or explicit foreground handoff semantics. - Do not add a local-only session index that diverges from daemon state. - Do not overload `⌘P` with generic mutating commands; that is `⌘K`. - Do not remove Sessions modal or add a rail until Island use is observed. - Do not impersonate macOS/iOS Dynamic Island visuals. Build an Ocean object using Ocean materials and behavior.

This is deliberately > concrete: data contracts, components, files, state transitions, keyboard > routing, CSS geometry, acceptance checks, and explicitly deferred work. > > The practical delivery sequence and commit gates live in > [`OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BUILD_PLAN.md`](OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BUILD_PLAN.md). ## Decision summary Build this before a permanent left rail. The first release is **not** a generalized desktop task system. It is a Tauri-only, titlebar-adjacent focus surface backed by the existing daemon session catalogue. ### V1 ships - compact Dynamic Island in the desktop header - focused session identity plus a count of active-background sessions - click to open an Island overlay - overlay lists active/recent sessions with project/path/branch/origin metadata - selecting a result calls the existing `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` and moves that session into the center transcript - `⌘P` opens that same overlay in search mode - fuzzy search over existing session metadata - arrow keys, Enter, Escape, click-outside behavior ### V1 does not ship - inline reply to a background session - cross-session live streaming in the Island - server-side/session-content semantic search - approvals, CI, GitHub, browser, rooms, Council, files, or PR results - a left rail - a replacement for the existing web/extension Sessions modal Those are follow-on waves after the core focus interaction is proven. ## Existing foundations to reuse Do not recreate these systems: | Existing implementation | Reuse in Island work | | --- | --- | | `Daemon::sessions: RwSignal>` | search corpus and list data | | `Daemon::session_id: RwSignal>` | focused-session identity | | `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` | sole session focus/switch operation | | `sessions.rs::split_origin`, `fmt_relative_time`, `session_root`, project lookup | display metadata and normalized search text | | `palette.rs::fuzzy_score` behavior | fuzzy scoring semantics; extract/move to a shared search helper rather than copy it | | `PaletteView` keyboard pattern | input autofocus, ArrowUp/Down, Enter, Escape, backdrop click | | `app.rs` `window_event_listener(ev::keydown, ...)` | `⌘P` global shortcut and overlay Escape priority | | `host::running_in_tauri()` | mount/gating boundary | | `styles/chrome.css` titlebar model | titlebar position and drag-region rules | Important fact: today `Daemon::switch_session` replaces the active transcript and reconnects its SSE/permission streams. The Island must call it; it must not attempt a second transcript/session runtime of its own. ## User-facing model ### Terminology - **Focused session**: the daemon's current `session_id`; it owns the center transcript and composer. - **Background session**: any other persisted session in the catalogue. V1 treats "recent" as the only reliable activity signal. - **Island**: compact titlebar control plus its expanded overlay. - **Search mode**: overlay opened by `⌘P`, with input focused. - **Browse mode**: overlay opened by click, with input present but not focused or visually secondary. Do not call every session "active" in V1. The client currently observes an SSE stream only for the focused session, so it cannot truthfully determine whether other sessions are presently generating work. Use **recent sessions** until the daemon publishes cross-session activity. ### V1 interaction flow ```text Focused center session: A Catalogue: A, B, C, D header Island (closed) [ A · Ocean Surface · 3 recent ] click Island OR press ⌘P → Island overlay opens → list shows A, B, C, D ordered by focus/recentness choose B + Enter/click → Daemon::switch_session(B.id, B.title) → B becomes focused center session → overlay closes → A remains in the catalogue and appears in future Island results ``` No extra "slotting" persistence is needed for V1. The natural catalogue order already makes the old focused session available. Explicit pins/orbits can arrive later only if observed usage requires them. ## Data model Create a new `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs` module. ### Core types ```rust #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum IslandMode { Closed, Browse, Search, } #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)] pub enum IslandPriority { Focused, Recent, Background, } #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub struct IslandSession { pub id: String, pub title: String, pub project: Option, pub cwd: String, pub branch: Option, pub origin: Option, pub updated_at: String, pub turn_count: u32, pub is_focused: bool, pub priority: IslandPriority, } #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] pub enum IslandResult { Session(IslandSession), } ``` Keep V1's result enum even though it has one variant. It establishes the extension seam for `Approval`, `BrowserTask`, `CiRun`, `File`, and `GitHubPull` without forcing speculative implementations today. ### Derivation function Expose a pure function in `island.rs`: ```rust pub(crate) fn derive_island_sessions( sessions: &[SessionSummary], projects: &[ProjectInfo], focused_id: Option<&str>, ) -> Vec; ``` Rules: 1. Retain every daemon-catalogued session, including zero-turn drafts. This follows `sessions.rs::group_for_panel` parity. 2. Resolve project display name via `owning_project`, then `project_for_root`. 3. Parse `[WEB]`, `[?]`, etc. title prefix using a reusable public helper from `sessions.rs` or a new shared metadata module. Do not duplicate parsing. 4. Sort: - focused session first, - then `updated_at` newest-first, - stable tie-breaker by title/id. 5. `priority` is `Focused` for focused session; `Recent` for sessions updated in the existing `is_recent` window; `Background` otherwise. 6. No claims about remote/live activity in V1. ### Search document and scoring Create a testable pure helper: ```rust pub(crate) fn island_search_text(item: &IslandSession) -> String; pub(crate) fn search_island( query: &str, items: &[IslandSession], ) -> Vec; ``` Search text joins, lowercased, with separators: ```text title project cwd branch origin state turns ``` Examples that must work: ```text north star project:ocean-surface // V1 literal text match is enough; facets deferred src/app.rs main tauri recent ``` Scoring: - empty query: existing derivation order - exact/prefix match in title: strongest boost - project match: second boost - cwd/branch/origin: normal fuzzy score - focused item: tie-break boost, not enough to hide better matches - recency: tie-break boost Extract `palette.rs::fuzzy_score` and the word-boundary helper into either: - `src/search.rs` (recommended), or - `pub(crate)` helpers in `palette.rs` Use the same scorer rather than making `⌘P` feel inconsistent with `⌘K`. ## Component API and ownership ### `Island` component ```rust #[component] pub fn Island( daemon: Daemon, mode: RwSignal, ) -> impl IntoView ``` `app.rs` owns `mode`, because it coordinates: - header click - `⌘P` - global Escape ordering - any future deep links / menu actions `Island` owns local overlay state: ```rust let query = RwSignal::new(String::new()); let selected_index = RwSignal::new(0usize); let input_ref = NodeRef::::new(); ``` ### Required component DOM shape ```text section.island-host // mounted inside .ocean-header button.island-chip // compact/default state focused session identity background/recent count state dot Show(mode != Closed) div.island-scrim // full window click target, below header section.island-popover // anchored below chip form / div island-search input.island-search__input div.island-results div.island-group button.island-result ``` Important: render `island-host` inside the header so the chip naturally occupies the titlebar zone. Render the scrim/popover with `position: fixed` and a high z-index so it is not clipped by the header and so its click-outside behavior is reliable. ### Compact chip behavior When no focused session exists: ```text Ocean · no session [open] ``` When focused session exists: ```text {title} · {project?} · {recent_count} recent ``` Constraints: - max compact width `520px` on wide desktop headers; responsive percentage and narrow-window caps must preserve both titlebar control zones - title line truncates - project is optional and truncates before title is hidden - no persistent animation unless attention becomes real in later slices - click toggles Browse; if Search is open, click closes - chip itself must not carry `data-tauri-drag-region` because it is interactive ### Overlay behavior - browse result limit: 8 initial rows (scroll beyond) - search result limit: 20 initial rows - result rows show: - title - project/path, branch, origin, relative time, turns - focused marker when applicable - click result: switch and close - no inline reply in V1 - background/scrim click: close ### Search-mode focus effect In `Island`, add an effect equivalent to `PaletteView`: ```rust Effect::new(move |_| { if mode.get() == IslandMode::Search { request_animation_frame(move || { if let Some(input) = input_ref.get() { let _ = input.focus(); input.select(); } }); } }); ``` Use the repo's existing rAF/focus utility if available; do not invent a setTimeout-based race. ## `app.rs` changes ### Imports and modules 1. Add `mod island;` in the crate root (`lib.rs` / module declaration location used by the project). 2. Import `Island`, `IslandMode` in `app.rs`. ### State Near `workspace_open` setup: ```rust let island_mode: RwSignal = RwSignal::new(IslandMode::Closed); let daemon_for_island = StoredValue::new(daemon.clone()); ``` No localStorage persistence in V1. An open overlay should not survive restart. ### Header mount Replace the Tauri interpretation of the current Sessions header trigger. Current code at `app.rs` roughly lines 958–971 renders a permanent labeled `Sessions` button. Change the header layout to: ```rust
...
... existing runtime + overflow + workspace controls ...
``` Do **not** move runtime status into the Island in V1. It already has stable presentation and should remain where it is. ### Shortcut routing Add a new focused listener before/alongside the current Escape listener: ```rust let _island_shortcut = window_event_listener(ev::keydown, move |e| { let is_cmd_p = (e.meta_key() || e.ctrl_key()) && !e.shift_key() && !e.alt_key() && e.key().eq_ignore_ascii_case("p"); if is_cmd_p && in_tauri { e.prevent_default(); e.stop_propagation(); island_mode.set(IslandMode::Search); } }); on_cleanup(move || _island_shortcut.remove()); ``` Use both Meta and Ctrl so the browser/PWA can share the behavior later if wanted, but gate initial mounting/handling on `in_tauri` to prevent intercepting browser print on non-Tauri hosts. ### Escape priority Update the existing global Escape ladder: ```text 1. PaletteView / Island local input handlers stop propagation themselves. 2. Council stage 3. Island overlay 4. Rooms 5. Sessions modal 6. Deck ``` The Island component's own input handler must call `stop_propagation()` on Escape after closing itself. The global handler only catches unhandled Escape from click/browse state. ### Sessions command Keep `toggle-sessions` unchanged in V1. It remains the deep browse fallback. Add a new command registry entry: ```rust Command { id: "focus-search", title: "Search Ocean…".into(), hint: Some("⌘P".into()), scope: CommandScope::App, slash: None, enabled: Signal::derive(move || in_tauri), run: Callback::new(move |_| island_mode.set(IslandMode::Search)), } ``` This makes the action discoverable in `⌘K` and native menubar work later while preserving the semantic separation: `⌘K` invokes the search surface; `⌘P` is the direct shortcut. ### No transcript/composer changes in V1 Do not remove the Sessions landing action or alter the composer in the Island first slice. The Island must prove useful before changing existing navigation fallbacks. ## Keyboard specification | Key | When Island input is focused | Behavior | | --- | --- | --- | | `⌘P` / `Ctrl+P` | anywhere in Tauri app | open/replace with Search mode; focus/select input | | `Esc` | search/browse overlay | close Island; prevent bubble | | `ArrowDown` | results non-empty | next result, wrapping | | `ArrowUp` | results non-empty | previous result, wrapping | | `Enter` | result selected | `switch_session`; close Island | | `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | search/browse overlay | keep focus in the combobox; results use `aria-activedescendant` | | click chip | closed | open Browse | | click chip | open | close | | click scrim | open | close | | click row | open | `switch_session`; close | Do not bind `⌘P` within a textarea only. It must work while transcript, composer, workspace, or header controls have focus. Respect IME composition if the app already exposes an equivalent guard; otherwise add it before intercepting the shortcut. ## CSS implementation Create `styles/island.css`; add it to `index.html` after `chrome.css` and before `panels.css`. Also add it to any explicit extension-style copy/build list only if the build requires every stylesheet to exist there. The component does not mount off-Tauri, so it remains visually inert on web/extension. ### Geometry tokens ```css :root { --island-max-w: 360px; --island-popover-w: min(560px, calc(100vw - 32px)); --island-top: 64px; /* header bottom + seam; revise against live Tauri shot */ } ``` ### Required layering ```text workspace pane 50 web deck 60 modal sessions 100 Island scrim/popover 120 command palette 1100 ``` The Island must sit above the workspace and ordinary panels, below `⌘K` palette. This means opening `⌘K` visually wins even if Island search is open; opening the palette should close Island as a small follow-up hardening task. ### Styling constraints - Island chip uses the existing OCEAN depth ramp, not iOS visual imitation. - No giant pill and no floating dashboard card. - Use a compact rounded capsule only because it communicates one living, titlebar-adjacent object. - Popover is a single elevated material surface with a crisp border; result rows use tone changes, not individually elevated cards. - Header must remain draggable around the Island. Keep left/right noninteractive zones as `data-tauri-drag-region`; explicitly omit it on chip, input, and rows. - At `< 840px` desktop width, reduce chip metadata to title + count. At widths too narrow for a usable popover, allow the fixed overlay to span the safe viewport width; do not introduce a different mobile design in this slice. ### Initial selectors ```css .ocean-header { position: relative; } .island-host { position: absolute; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); } .island-chip { /* compact titlebar control */ } .island-scrim { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 120; } .island-popover { position: fixed; z-index: 121; top: var(--island-top); left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); } .island-search__input { /* palette-like focus treatment */ } .island-result { /* one full-width interactive row */ } .island-result--selected { /* selected keyboard row */ } .island-result--focused { /* understated current-session marker */ } ``` Do not use `overflow: hidden` on `.ocean-header`; it would clip the popover. ## File-by-file change list | Path | Change | | --- | --- | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/lib.rs` or current module root | declare `mod island;` | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs` | new pure derivation/search helpers + `Island` component + tests | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/app.rs` | Island state, header mount, `⌘P`, Escape priority, registry command | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/sessions.rs` | expose/shared metadata helpers only if needed; do not move panel UI | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/palette.rs` | move fuzzy scorer to a shared module or expose it safely; no duplicated score algorithm | | `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/search.rs` | recommended new shared fuzzy scorer if extraction is clean | | `styles/island.css` | new Island geometry and skin | | `index.html` | add stylesheet link | | extension build/style wiring | only if stylesheet packaging explicitly requires it | | `docs/OCEAN_DESKTOP_NORTH_STAR.md` | already records product direction; add implementation-doc link if docs use a links section | ## Tests ### Unit tests in `island.rs` - focused session sorts first - newer background sessions sort before older sessions - project derives from `owning_project` - project falls back to workspace-root match - origin prefix is stripped from title and exposed separately - title query beats project/path-only fuzzy query - empty query preserves derived order - `recent` / state text appears in searchable text if the chosen V1 behavior supports literal state queries - zero-turn session remains searchable ### Existing regression checks - `sessions.rs` grouping tests remain unchanged and pass - `palette.rs` fuzzy tests pass after helper extraction - verify `Daemon::switch_session` remains the only focus switch path ### Manual desktop acceptance run 1. Start Tauri app with ≥4 persisted sessions across ≥2 projects. 2. Verify chip is centered and does not overlap traffic lights, runtime controls, or workspace toggle. 3. Click chip: browse overlay opens, shows focused session first. 4. Click outside: closes. 5. Press `⌘P` from composer, workspace, and header: search opens and input has focus each time. 6. Type project, branch, title, cwd, and origin queries; confirm expected result. 7. Arrow down/up/Enter switches session and overlay closes. 8. Confirm old session is available when opening Island again. 9. Confirm `⌘K` palette still works and Escape closes exactly the topmost open surface. 10. Resize Tauri to narrow and wide widths; verify usable overlay geometry. 11. Verify browser PWA and extension preserve their existing Sessions-modal and browser-print behavior. ## Build sequence / commits Do not put all behavior in one giant commit. ### Commit 1 — Pure Island index - new `island.rs` types/derivation/search helpers - extract shared fuzzy score - unit tests only - no UI **Exit:** `cargo test` for the UI crate passes. ### Commit 2 — Island visual shell - component mounts on Tauri header - closed/browse state - display derived session rows - click row switches session - CSS and stylesheet wiring **Exit:** click-only interaction works; web has no visual change. ### Commit 3 — `⌘P` search mode - global shortcut - search input/focus - filtering, selection, keyboard navigation - Escape priority - registry discoverability command **Exit:** keyboard-only session focus switching works. ### Commit 4 — Live desktop polish - inspect an actual Tauri screenshot - tune titlebar spacing, type scale, row density, result limit, focus ring - run narrow/wide regressions **Exit:** the control feels built into the native shell rather than pasted over web chrome. ## Follow-up contract: required daemon work before richer Island states Do not fake background activity with only timestamps. For V2+ Island items, request an explicit daemon-owned stream/snapshot that can represent cross-session work truth: ```rust struct WorkAttentionItem { id: String, kind: Session | Permission | Browser | Ci | GitHub | Room | Council, session_id: Option, title: String, detail: Option, state: Idle | Running | NeedsHuman | Failed | Complete, updated_at: String, priority: u8, } ``` The daemon should own the source of truth. The Island is a reducer/view of that stream. This preserves the existing many-surfaces-one-daemon architecture and prevents a Tauri-only notion of work state. ## Explicit non-goal guardrails - Do not build inline quick reply until the daemon supports a safe background session prompt lifecycle or explicit foreground handoff semantics. - Do not add a local-only session index that diverges from daemon state. - Do not overload `⌘P` with generic mutating commands; that is `⌘K`. - Do not remove Sessions modal or add a rail until Island use is observed. - Do not impersonate macOS/iOS Dynamic Island visuals. Build an Ocean object using Ocean materials and behavior.

# Dynamic Island + `⌘P` — Build Plan

> Practical delivery sequence for implementing
> [`OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`](OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_IMPLEMENTATION.md).
> This document describes how to start, what to build first, commit boundaries,
> verification gates, and when to introduce richer daemon-backed attention
> state.

## Goal

Start with a thin vertical slice that proves one complete interaction:

> **Press `⌘P` → find a session → press Enter → that session takes over the
> focused transcript.**

Once that loop is reliable and feels good, mount the same machinery in the
ambient titlebar Island. Do not attempt the entire long-term Island vision in
one pass.

## Step 0 — Protect the current worktree

The current worktree already contains unrelated modifications, including:

- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/sessions.rs`
- `crates/ocean-tauri/src/lib.rs`

Before implementation:

1. Inspect the existing diffs.
2. Determine whether they belong to another active change.
3. Create a dedicated branch or worktree for the Island build if appropriate.
4. Keep the North Star and implementation documents with the Island work.
5. Do not overwrite or revert unrelated modifications.

This prevents the titlebar/session architecture work from being mixed with an
unrelated Tauri or sessions change.

## Step 1 — Build the pure session-search model

Start with code that has no DOM, CSS, or Tauri dependency.

### Files

Add:

- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/search.rs`
- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs`

Update the crate's module declarations as required.

### Implement

- shared fuzzy scoring extracted from `palette.rs`
- `IslandMode`
- `IslandSession`
- `IslandResult`
- `derive_island_sessions(...)`
- `island_search_text(...)`
- `search_island(...)`
- title/project/path/branch/origin normalization
- deterministic result ordering

### Reuse

Use the existing sources of truth:

- `Daemon::sessions`
- `Daemon::projects`
- `Daemon::session_id`
- `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)`
- project ownership helpers from `sessions.rs`
- session-root and origin parsing from `sessions.rs`
- fuzzy-search behavior from `palette.rs`

Do not duplicate project matching, origin parsing, or fuzzy-scoring algorithms.
Extract or safely expose shared helpers.

### Truth constraint

V1 may identify sessions as:

- focused
- recent
- background

It must not claim background sessions are actively running or waiting for a
reply. The client currently has complete live runtime observation only for the
focused session.

### Unit-test exit criteria

Tests must prove:

- focused session ranks first for an empty query
- newer background sessions sort before older sessions
- title matches outrank path-only matches
- project name is searchable
- cwd path is searchable
- branch is searchable
- origin is searchable
- zero-turn sessions remain discoverable
- origin prefixes are formatted correctly
- empty query preserves derived ordering
- result ordering is deterministic

## Step 2 — Build `⌘P` as a minimal focus switcher

Before designing the ambient chip, prove the core interaction.

### Add a minimal Island overlay

The overlay must:

- open when `⌘P` is pressed in Tauri
- fetch current sessions and projects when opened
- focus and select its search input
- show filtered session results
- support ArrowUp and ArrowDown
- support Enter to select
- support Escape to close
- close when its backdrop is clicked
- call `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` for the selected session
- close after a successful switch

The existing Sessions panel already calls:

- `Daemon::fetch_sessions()`
- `Daemon::fetch_projects()`

The Island should use those same methods when Browse or Search mode opens, so it
does not operate on a stale catalogue.

### Shortcut behavior

Initial behavior:

- `⌘P` on macOS opens Search mode
- `Ctrl+P` may be supported for parity
- intercept the shortcut only on Tauri for V1
- do not intercept browser/PWA Print behavior
- the shortcut must work while focus is in the composer, transcript, workspace,
  or header

### Keyboard behavior

| Key | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `⌘P` / `Ctrl+P` | Open Search mode and focus/select the input |
| `Escape` | Close Island and stop propagation |
| `ArrowDown` | Select next result, wrapping |
| `ArrowUp` | Select previous result, wrapping |
| `Enter` | Focus selected session and close |
| `Tab` | Use normal focus traversal in V1 |

### Exit criteria

From any focused area in Tauri:

1. Press `⌘P`.
2. Type part of a session title, project, path, branch, or origin.
3. Navigate with ArrowUp/ArrowDown.
4. Press Enter.
5. Confirm the selected transcript loads.
6. Open `⌘P` again and confirm the old session remains discoverable.
7. Confirm the browser/PWA still retains its normal Print shortcut.

This milestone is the first complete product proof.

## Step 3 — Add the compact titlebar Island

After the search/focus loop works, mount the compact Island inside
`.ocean-header` on Tauri only.

### Compact content

Initially show:

- focused session title
- project name when space permits
- number of recent background sessions
- a subtle state dot

When no session is focused, show a quiet empty state such as:

```text
Ocean · no session
```

### Interaction

- clicking the compact Island opens Browse mode
- clicking while it is open closes it
- Browse mode uses the same overlay and result pipeline as Search mode
- selecting a session switches focus and closes the overlay

### Initial visual constraints

- maximum compact width: approximately `520px` on wide desktop headers, with narrower breakpoint caps
- truncate metadata before obscuring the session title
- do not add urgency animation without truthful attention data
- do not use multiple decorative chips in V1
- do not add hover expansion yet
- do not add inline reply yet
- the Island must not carry `data-tauri-drag-region`
- the surrounding header must remain draggable

### Exit criteria

- Island is centered cleanly in the live Tauri titlebar
- it does not overlap macOS traffic lights
- it does not overlap runtime telemetry, overflow, or workspace controls
- the Island remains interactive
- surrounding titlebar space still drags the window
- narrow windows truncate gracefully
- the web and extension surfaces do not mount the Island

## Step 4 — Unify Browse and Search modes

Use one component, one overlay, and one result pipeline.

Do not build a separate Island dropdown and quick-open palette.

### Browse mode

Opened by clicking the compact Island:

- focused session first
- recent sessions next
- search input may remain visible but visually secondary
- initial list can be limited to approximately eight visible rows
- scrolling exposes additional results

### Search mode

Opened by `⌘P`:

- input receives focus immediately
- existing query is selected or cleared according to the final interaction
  decision
- fuzzy filtering begins immediately
- first result is selected
- up to approximately twenty initial search results may be rendered

### State model

```rust
pub enum IslandMode {
    Closed,
    Browse,
    Search,
}
```

`app.rs` owns `IslandMode`, because global shortcuts and Escape ordering are
application-level concerns. The `Island` component owns local query and keyboard
selection state.

## Step 5 — Polish from the real Tauri application

Do not approve the visual treatment from generic mockups.

After the feature runs:

1. Launch the real Tauri app.
2. Capture the actual native window.
3. Test both narrow and wide window sizes.
4. Tune titlebar position and control spacing.
5. Tune typography and metadata density.
6. Remove any styling that resembles a floating web modal.
7. Verify the Island reads as one Ocean object rather than an imitation of
   Apple's iPhone Dynamic Island.

### Visual principles

- use Ocean's existing depth ramp and cyan/teal cues
- compact capsule is acceptable because it represents one living titlebar object
- use one elevated popover surface
- use tonal result-row selection rather than individually elevated cards
- avoid unnecessary shadows, pills, and nested rounded containers
- preserve the titlebar's native drag behavior

## Step 6 — Observe before expanding the product

Use the session-focused V1 before adding broad integrations.

Questions to answer from actual use:

- How many sessions are useful in the Island at once?
- Is click-to-browse useful, or does `⌘P` dominate?
- Should the focused session remain visible in the compact Island?
- Do operators want explicit pins or only recent work?
- Is inline reply better than switching focus?
- Does a rail remain necessary for deep project browsing?
- Which metadata is useful versus noisy?

Do not answer these questions through speculative UI alone.

## Step 7 — Add real attention state through the daemon

The richer Island vision requires daemon-owned cross-session truth.

The current client cannot reliably know whether a background session is:

- running
- waiting for a reply
- blocked on approval
- failed
- complete

Do not infer these states from timestamps.

### Proposed follow-up daemon contract

```rust
struct WorkAttentionItem {
    id: String,
    kind: WorkKind,
    session_id: Option<String>,
    title: String,
    detail: Option<String>,
    state: WorkState,
    updated_at: String,
    priority: u8,
}

enum WorkKind {
    Session,
    Permission,
    Browser,
    Ci,
    GitHub,
    Room,
    Council,
}

enum WorkState {
    Idle,
    Running,
    NeedsHuman,
    Failed,
    Complete,
}
```

The daemon owns the source of truth. The Island reduces and renders that state.
This preserves Ocean's many-surfaces-one-daemon architecture.

### Suggested integration order

After daemon support exists:

1. permission requests
2. background session execution
3. browser-driving work
4. CI and GitHub runs
5. Council / Longhouse activity
6. calls and rooms

## Commit sequence

Keep each commit independently understandable and testable.

### Commit 1 — Search core

Changes:

- shared fuzzy scorer
- Island data types
- session derivation
- search functions
- unit tests

Verification:

- focused UI-crate tests
- existing palette fuzzy tests
- existing session grouping tests

### Commit 2 — `⌘P` focus switcher

Changes:

- Island overlay
- session/project refresh on open
- input and result list
- keyboard behavior
- session switching
- Escape/backdrop handling

Verification:

- keyboard-only focus switch works in Tauri
- browser Print remains unaffected

### Commit 3 — Compact titlebar Island

Changes:

- Tauri-only header mount
- Browse mode
- focused title/project/recent count
- `styles/island.css`
- stylesheet wiring

Verification:

- native header interaction and drag-region checks
- no web/extension visual changes

### Commit 4 — Native polish and hardening

# Dynamic Island + `⌘P` — Build Plan

> Practical delivery sequence for implementing
> [`OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`](OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_IMPLEMENTATION.md).
> This document describes how to start, what to build first, commit boundaries,
> verification gates, and when to introduce richer daemon-backed attention
> state.

## Goal

Start with a thin vertical slice that proves one complete interaction:

> **Press `⌘P` → find a session → press Enter → that session takes over the
> focused transcript.**

Once that loop is reliable and feels good, mount the same machinery in the
ambient titlebar Island. Do not attempt the entire long-term Island vision in
one pass.

## Step 0 — Protect the current worktree

The current worktree already contains unrelated modifications, including:

- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/sessions.rs`
- `crates/ocean-tauri/src/lib.rs`

Before implementation:

1. Inspect the existing diffs.
2. Determine whether they belong to another active change.
3. Create a dedicated branch or worktree for the Island build if appropriate.
4. Keep the North Star and implementation documents with the Island work.
5. Do not overwrite or revert unrelated modifications.

This prevents the titlebar/session architecture work from being mixed with an
unrelated Tauri or sessions change.

## Step 1 — Build the pure session-search model

Start with code that has no DOM, CSS, or Tauri dependency.

### Files

Add:

- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/search.rs`
- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs`

Update the crate's module declarations as required.

### Implement

- shared fuzzy scoring extracted from `palette.rs`
- `IslandMode`
- `IslandSession`
- `IslandResult`
- `derive_island_sessions(...)`
- `island_search_text(...)`
- `search_island(...)`
- title/project/path/branch/origin normalization
- deterministic result ordering

### Reuse

Use the existing sources of truth:

- `Daemon::sessions`
- `Daemon::projects`
- `Daemon::session_id`
- `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)`
- project ownership helpers from `sessions.rs`
- session-root and origin parsing from `sessions.rs`
- fuzzy-search behavior from `palette.rs`

Do not duplicate project matching, origin parsing, or fuzzy-scoring algorithms.
Extract or safely expose shared helpers.

### Truth constraint

V1 may identify sessions as:

- focused
- recent
- background

It must not claim background sessions are actively running or waiting for a
reply. The client currently has complete live runtime observation only for the
focused session.

### Unit-test exit criteria

Tests must prove:

- focused session ranks first for an empty query
- newer background sessions sort before older sessions
- title matches outrank path-only matches
- project name is searchable
- cwd path is searchable
- branch is searchable
- origin is searchable
- zero-turn sessions remain discoverable
- origin prefixes are formatted correctly
- empty query preserves derived ordering
- result ordering is deterministic

## Step 2 — Build `⌘P` as a minimal focus switcher

Before designing the ambient chip, prove the core interaction.

### Add a minimal Island overlay

The overlay must:

- open when `⌘P` is pressed in Tauri
- fetch current sessions and projects when opened
- focus and select its search input
- show filtered session results
- support ArrowUp and ArrowDown
- support Enter to select
- support Escape to close
- close when its backdrop is clicked
- call `Daemon::switch_session(id, title)` for the selected session
- close after a successful switch

The existing Sessions panel already calls:

- `Daemon::fetch_sessions()`
- `Daemon::fetch_projects()`

The Island should use those same methods when Browse or Search mode opens, so it
does not operate on a stale catalogue.

### Shortcut behavior

Initial behavior:

- `⌘P` on macOS opens Search mode
- `Ctrl+P` may be supported for parity
- intercept the shortcut only on Tauri for V1
- do not intercept browser/PWA Print behavior
- the shortcut must work while focus is in the composer, transcript, workspace,
  or header

### Keyboard behavior

| Key | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `⌘P` / `Ctrl+P` | Open Search mode and focus/select the input |
| `Escape` | Close Island and stop propagation |
| `ArrowDown` | Select next result, wrapping |
| `ArrowUp` | Select previous result, wrapping |
| `Enter` | Focus selected session and close |
| `Tab` | Use normal focus traversal in V1 |

### Exit criteria

From any focused area in Tauri:

1. Press `⌘P`.
2. Type part of a session title, project, path, branch, or origin.
3. Navigate with ArrowUp/ArrowDown.
4. Press Enter.
5. Confirm the selected transcript loads.
6. Open `⌘P` again and confirm the old session remains discoverable.
7. Confirm the browser/PWA still retains its normal Print shortcut.

This milestone is the first complete product proof.

## Step 3 — Add the compact titlebar Island

After the search/focus loop works, mount the compact Island inside
`.ocean-header` on Tauri only.

### Compact content

Initially show:

- focused session title
- project name when space permits
- number of recent background sessions
- a subtle state dot

When no session is focused, show a quiet empty state such as:

```text
Ocean · no session
```

### Interaction

- clicking the compact Island opens Browse mode
- clicking while it is open closes it
- Browse mode uses the same overlay and result pipeline as Search mode
- selecting a session switches focus and closes the overlay

### Initial visual constraints

- maximum compact width: approximately `520px` on wide desktop headers, with narrower breakpoint caps
- truncate metadata before obscuring the session title
- do not add urgency animation without truthful attention data
- do not use multiple decorative chips in V1
- do not add hover expansion yet
- do not add inline reply yet
- the Island must not carry `data-tauri-drag-region`
- the surrounding header must remain draggable

### Exit criteria

- Island is centered cleanly in the live Tauri titlebar
- it does not overlap macOS traffic lights
- it does not overlap runtime telemetry, overflow, or workspace controls
- the Island remains interactive
- surrounding titlebar space still drags the window
- narrow windows truncate gracefully
- the web and extension surfaces do not mount the Island

## Step 4 — Unify Browse and Search modes

Use one component, one overlay, and one result pipeline.

Do not build a separate Island dropdown and quick-open palette.

### Browse mode

Opened by clicking the compact Island:

- focused session first
- recent sessions next
- search input may remain visible but visually secondary
- initial list can be limited to approximately eight visible rows
- scrolling exposes additional results

### Search mode

Opened by `⌘P`:

- input receives focus immediately
- existing query is selected or cleared according to the final interaction
  decision
- fuzzy filtering begins immediately
- first result is selected
- up to approximately twenty initial search results may be rendered

### State model

```rust
pub enum IslandMode {
    Closed,
    Browse,
    Search,
}
```

`app.rs` owns `IslandMode`, because global shortcuts and Escape ordering are
application-level concerns. The `Island` component owns local query and keyboard
selection state.

## Step 5 — Polish from the real Tauri application

Do not approve the visual treatment from generic mockups.

After the feature runs:

1. Launch the real Tauri app.
2. Capture the actual native window.
3. Test both narrow and wide window sizes.
4. Tune titlebar position and control spacing.
5. Tune typography and metadata density.
6. Remove any styling that resembles a floating web modal.
7. Verify the Island reads as one Ocean object rather than an imitation of
   Apple's iPhone Dynamic Island.

### Visual principles

- use Ocean's existing depth ramp and cyan/teal cues
- compact capsule is acceptable because it represents one living titlebar object
- use one elevated popover surface
- use tonal result-row selection rather than individually elevated cards
- avoid unnecessary shadows, pills, and nested rounded containers
- preserve the titlebar's native drag behavior

## Step 6 — Observe before expanding the product

Use the session-focused V1 before adding broad integrations.

Questions to answer from actual use:

- How many sessions are useful in the Island at once?
- Is click-to-browse useful, or does `⌘P` dominate?
- Should the focused session remain visible in the compact Island?
- Do operators want explicit pins or only recent work?
- Is inline reply better than switching focus?
- Does a rail remain necessary for deep project browsing?
- Which metadata is useful versus noisy?

Do not answer these questions through speculative UI alone.

## Step 7 — Add real attention state through the daemon

The richer Island vision requires daemon-owned cross-session truth.

The current client cannot reliably know whether a background session is:

- running
- waiting for a reply
- blocked on approval
- failed
- complete

Do not infer these states from timestamps.

### Proposed follow-up daemon contract

```rust
struct WorkAttentionItem {
    id: String,
    kind: WorkKind,
    session_id: Option<String>,
    title: String,
    detail: Option<String>,
    state: WorkState,
    updated_at: String,
    priority: u8,
}

enum WorkKind {
    Session,
    Permission,
    Browser,
    Ci,
    GitHub,
    Room,
    Council,
}

enum WorkState {
    Idle,
    Running,
    NeedsHuman,
    Failed,
    Complete,
}
```

The daemon owns the source of truth. The Island reduces and renders that state.
This preserves Ocean's many-surfaces-one-daemon architecture.

### Suggested integration order

After daemon support exists:

1. permission requests
2. background session execution
3. browser-driving work
4. CI and GitHub runs
5. Council / Longhouse activity
6. calls and rooms

## Commit sequence

Keep each commit independently understandable and testable.

### Commit 1 — Search core

Changes:

- shared fuzzy scorer
- Island data types
- session derivation
- search functions
- unit tests

Verification:

- focused UI-crate tests
- existing palette fuzzy tests
- existing session grouping tests

### Commit 2 — `⌘P` focus switcher

Changes:

- Island overlay
- session/project refresh on open
- input and result list
- keyboard behavior
- session switching
- Escape/backdrop handling

Verification:

- keyboard-only focus switch works in Tauri
- browser Print remains unaffected

### Commit 3 — Compact titlebar Island

Changes:

- Tauri-only header mount
- Browse mode
- focused title/project/recent count
- `styles/island.css`
- stylesheet wiring

Verification:

- native header interaction and drag-region checks
- no web/extension visual changes

### Commit 4 — Native polish and hardening

Changes:

- screenshot-based visual refinement
- narrow/wide layout behavior
- z-index and Escape ordering
- coexistence with `⌘K`
- accessibility labels and focus states

Verification:

- manual Tauri acceptance pass
- focused Rust/WASM checks
- web and extension regression pass

## File-level plan

| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/search.rs` | shared fuzzy matcher extracted from palette logic |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs` | Island types, derivation, search, component, unit tests |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/app.rs` | `IslandMode`, Tauri mount, `⌘P`, Escape priority, registry command |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/sessions.rs` | expose reusable metadata/project helpers where needed |
| `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/palette.rs` | consume shared fuzzy scorer after extraction |
| `styles/island.css` | compact Island, overlay, results, responsive geometry |
| `styles/chrome.css` | titlebar positioning adjustments only if required |
| `index.html` | Island stylesheet link |
| extension build/style wiring | update only if explicit stylesheet packaging requires it |

## First coding task

Start with **Commit 1: the pure session-search core**.

It is the best entry point because it is:

- low risk
- independently testable
- free from premature visual decisions
- reusable by Browse and Search modes
- compatible with future Island entities
- unlikely to disturb the existing web/extension UX

The first implementation session should end with tested Rust helpers—not a
partially working visual overlay.

## Definition of V1 complete

V1 is complete when:

- Tauri shows a compact Island in the header
- clicking the Island opens Browse mode
- `⌘P` opens Search mode from anywhere in the app
- sessions can be searched by existing metadata

text: # Ocean Web Surface — Design System Authority for all visual work in the Leptos web surface (`crates/ocean-surface-ui`, `styles/*.css`, `index.html`). Ocean's OWN identity — not an agency re-brand — applied at **product register**: the UI serves the task; brand energy is rationed, never decorative. Register rule: a user fluent in Linear/Figma/Raycast should trust every control on sight. Familiar affordances, one component vocabulary, restrained color. **Control density is a design defect.** The surface holds exactly the controls the current moment needs; everything else is conditional, collapsed behind one overflow, or revealed on intent (hover/focus). A row of same-weight buttons is failure — one primary affordance, quiet metadata, ghost triggers. ## 1. Identity The OCEAN depth ramp comes from the ASCII splash banner in the TUI (`ocean-os/crates/ocean-tui/src/splash.rs`), deep indigo rising to bright aqua (xterm 17→19→25→31→38→44→50→87). The active logo direction is now the circular neumorphic wave mark, not the ASCII banner and not a terminal prompt glyph. Reference asset: `public/brand/master-1024.png` (mirrored as `public/brand/ocean-mark.svg`). Logo implementation target: - Replace the current three-line `WaveLogo` and text-only header wordmark with an inline SVG circular mark component that preserves the reference geometry: circular badge, stacked wave cutouts, teal-to-blue depth ramp, matte dark relief, and shallow inner/outer shadow. - Keep the SVG inline in the Leptos bundle, not as ``, so the same asset can animate in web and Tauri. Name internal layers (`rim`, `wave-1`, `wave-2`, `wave-3`, `deep-water`, `wordmark`) so CSS can target state motion. - Test three lockups before choosing: mark-only, lowercase `ocean`, and tighter uppercase `OCEAN` with less spacing than the current landing wordmark. - Avoid prompt/code symbolism completely: no `>`, `_`, cursor, brackets, terminal glyphs, sparkle/star motifs, mascots, or Codex-adjacent shapes. - Tauri consumes the same Trunk-built Leptos bundle, so the web logo component is the primary fix for both browser and native shell. Generate Tauri app icons from the final mark only after the web lockup is accepted. Never gradient-clip text. The ramp is always painted as solid colors on discrete elements, or as vector fills inside the circular mark. The page is near-black; the working accent (`--ocean-6` cyan) appears ONLY at: - Primary actions (send, approve, join, submit, create) — solid cyan fill with dark ink (`--fg-on-accent`), never white text, never a gradient fill. - Live/active states: voice orb recording, speaking ring, live dots, active selection fills. - Focus rings (single cyan ring). Everything else is neutral: near-black surfaces, low-opacity white borders, the near-white/grey text ramp. No teal-mint (legacy #7fe7c8), no navy chrome, no magenta/purple (rejected 2026-07-04). ## 2. Tokens (`styles/tokens.css` — the only place colors are defined) Surfaces - `--bg: #060606` page - `--bg-raised: #0A0A0A` bars, panels, drawers - `--bg-elevated: #141414` cards, inputs, chips, wells - `--bg-hover: #1B1C21` hover fill on elevated surfaces - `--bg-well: #23252B` special data wells (code, diff, transcript wells) Text - `--fg: #FAFCFF` headings, primary content - `--fg-2: #B8B9BB` body secondary - `--fg-3: #909098` labels, metadata - `--fg-4: #5A5C63` disabled only — never for readable content Brand — the OCEAN ramp - `--ocean-1..8`: `#00005F #0000AF #005FAF #0087AF #00AFD7 #00D7D7 #00FFD7 #5FFFFF` (identity surfaces only: banner rows, wordmark letters, data-fill gradient) - `--accent: var(--ocean-6)` interactive accent (links, active text, hot states) - `--accent-bright: var(--ocean-7)` live highlights - `--accent-deep: var(--ocean-4)` depth end of data gradients - `--fg-on-accent: #03181A` ink on accent fills — accent fills NEVER take white text - `--gradient: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--ocean-6), var(--ocean-4))` DATA fills (chart bars) only — never buttons, never text - `--accent-soft: rgba(0,215,215,0.12)` tinted fills - `--accent-ring: rgba(0,215,215,0.45)` focus ring color Status (semantic; used for tool state, call state, deltas, diffs) - `--ok: #1ED760`, `--ok-soft: rgba(30, 215, 96, 0.12)` - `--err: #FF4D67`, `--err-soft: rgba(255, 77, 103, 0.12)` - `--warn: #FFB224`, `--warn-soft: rgba(255, 178, 36, 0.12)` - `--info: #6AA6FF`, `--info-soft: rgba(106, 166, 255, 0.12)` - `--running: var(--warn)` (in-flight tool state) Borders - `--border-subtle: rgba(255,255,255,0.06)` - `--border: rgba(255,255,255,0.10)` - `--border-strong: rgba(255,255,255,0.20)` Type - `--font: 'Poppins', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif` - `--mono: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace` - Scale (fixed px, product register): 11 label / 12 small / 13 secondary / 14 body / 15 emphasized / 18 title / 22 display. Body line-height 1.55. - Uppercase labels: 11px, weight 600, `letter-spacing: 0.08em`, `--fg-3`. - Mono is for DATA (paths, ids, tokens, numbers, code), never for UI labels. Radii — pill is GEOMETRY, never chrome - `--radius-sm: 4px` chips, badges, tabs, menu items, mono data chips - `--radius: 6px` inputs, buttons, selects, list rows, dropdown menus - `--radius-lg: 10px` cards, panels, modals, composer dock - `--radius-pill: 999px` true circles/capsules ONLY: status dots, the voice orb, progress bars, scrollbar thumbs. Never on a text-bearing control — pill buttons/inputs/chips read 2015-SaaS and are banned (2026-07-06). Shadows / glow - `--shadow-sm: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.40)` - `--shadow-md: 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.55)` - `--shadow-lg: 0 24px 64px rgba(0,0,0,0.65)` overlays/slide-overs only - `--glow-brand: 0 0 32px rgba(0,215,215,0.28)` voice orb / live moments only Material — molded from the digital ocean - `--specular: rgba(255,255,255,0.08)` top-edge light on raised surfaces - `--specular-soft: rgba(255,255,255,0.05)` fainter top-edge (elev-1 rows/controls) - `--specular-live: rgba(95,255,255,0.16)` aqua specular for live/active states - `--elev-1` inset specular-soft + tight drop — controls, menu rows, chips - `--elev-2` inset specular + mid drop — cards, docks, list panels - `--elev-3` inset specular + deep drop — popovers, modals, tooltips - `--well` inset shadow + faint bottom specular — inputs, data/code wells - `--well-deep` deeper inset — deepest wells (transcript, diff bodies) - `--pressed: inset 0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.60)` :active pressed-in - `--glow-thinking: 0 0 24px rgba(0,215,215,0.10)` breathing cognition glow - `--glow-live: 0 0 20px rgba(0,255,215,0.16)` active-streaming glow - `--pointer-x / --pointer-y: 50%` pointer-light origin (root listener writes) - `--pointer-light: rgba(95,255,255,0.04)` faint radial specular at pointer Motion - `--ease: cubic-bezier(.22,.61,.36,1)`; `--dur-fast: 160ms`; `--dur: 240ms`; `--dur-slow: 420ms`; `--ease-tide: cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.28,1)` rise-from-depth (tidal entrance curve). - Motion conveys state only. No bounce, no elastic, no decorative entrance choreography — the ONLY entrance allowed is the tidal rise for overlays/popovers (see Material). - EVERY animation gets a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` kill. Controls & layout - `--ctl-h: 34px` standard control height; `--ctl-h-sm: 28px` compact chips - `--focus-ring: 0 0 0 2px var(--accent-ring)` - `--shell-max: 1120px` desktop shell width ## 3. Control recipes (the ONE vocabulary — every domain uses these verbatim) The reference component is the header overflow menu (`ocean-more__menu`): an elevated panel, hairline border, tight radius, plain text rows — no icons, no subtitles, no accent chrome. Every new component must justify any element that menu doesn't have (an icon lockup, a subtitle, a fill) before adding it. Primary button (send, approve, submit, join, create): - `background: var(--accent)`, `color: var(--fg-on-accent)` (dark ink — never white), weight 600, `--radius`, compact height (`--ctl-h-sm` in docks), padding 0 14px, border: none. - Hover: `filter: brightness(1.12)`. Press: `transform: scale(0.985)`. - Disabled: `opacity: 0.45`, no pointer events. Secondary button (cancel, leave, toggles, header actions): - `background: var(--bg-elevated)`, `1px solid var(--border)`, `--fg` text, `--radius`, height `--ctl-h`. - Hover: `background: var(--bg-hover); border-color: var(--border-strong)`. - NEVER pair a border with a wide soft shadow. Ghost button (icon buttons, close ×, drawer heads): - Transparent bg, `--fg-3` content; hover: `--bg-elevated` fill + `--fg`. Danger: secondary shape with `--err` text; fill `--err-soft` on hover. Deny/halt follows danger; approve follows primary. Inputs & textareas: - `background: var(--bg-raised)`, `1px solid var(--border)`, `--radius`, `--fg` text, placeholder `--fg-3` (not dimmer). - Focus: `border-color: var(--accent); box-shadow: var(--focus-ring)`; no outline. Selects (project picker, thinking, model, form selects): - `appearance: none` + the recipe above + custom chevron as inline `background-image` SVG (stroke `#909098`), `background-position: right 10px center`, padding-right 30px. Same height as buttons. Sans font, NOT mono. Chips/badges: `--radius-sm`, `--bg-elevated` + `--border-subtle`, 12px text. State chips tint with the matching `*-soft` bg + solid status text. Focus: `:focus-visible { box-shadow: var(--focus-ring); outline: none; }` on all interactive elements. Never remove focus affordance without replacing it. Scrollbars: keep the existing thin overlay treatment, thumb `rgba(255,255,255,0.12)`, hover `rgba(255,255,255,0.22)`. No accent scrollbars. Failure surfaces: - Status chip (`.ocean-status`): one short line, state-label register (`turn failed: `), NEVER raw payloads/JSON/multi-line text; source normalizes before set — CSS ellipsis is only a guard. - Full error payloads go to the console log and (when a turn/tool errored) render as expanded Err tool blocks in the transcript — the transcript is the detail carrier, the chip is the signal. - Failed user turns must never dangle silently: the failure must be visible in status AND recoverable (input preserved, resend possible). - Errors follow voice rules: explain what went wrong in the interface voice, never vague, no apology. ## Material — molded from the digital ocean One overhead light source. RAISED surfaces catch a top-edge specular (`--specular`) and cast a dark drop below; CARVED wells fall away into darker water. Elevation replaces borders — an element takes the border recipe OR the elevation recipe, never both. Agent cognition is bioluminescence: existing state hooks (`is-*` classes, data attrs the Rust already emits) drive the glow tokens — no new state plumbing, only new declarations on hooks that already exist. RAISED — interactive controls, cards, popovers: - `box-shadow: var(--elev-N)`: `--elev-1` controls/rows/chips, `--elev-2` cards/docks/list panels, `--elev-3` popovers/modals/tooltips. - REMOVE any 1px border on the same element — the specular inset replaces the outline. (The §5 "1px border + ≥16px blur" ban stands.) CARVED — inputs, code/diff/data wells: - Darker bg (`--bg-well`, deeper for the deepest wells) + `box-shadow: var(--well)` (or `--well-deep`). PRESSED — `:active` on raised controls: - `box-shadow: var(--pressed); transform: translateY(1px)`. The focus ring (`--focus-ring`) is unchanged and stacks with elevation. Bioluminescence state map — attach to existing hooks only: - Thinking: `--glow-thinking`, a slow breathing keyframe (opacity/scale). - Tool running: lift `--elev-1` → `--elev-2` and brighten to `--specular-live`. - Streaming: materialize — incoming content fades/translates in on the tide. - Permission wait: `--warn` ring pulse over a `--warn-soft` fill. - Live call: `--accent` dot pulse. The live-state color map holds everywhere — live = `--accent` pulse, connected = `--ok`, reconnecting = `--warn`, failed/barge = `--err`. Agent-response loading: - Replace the current pending-response sonar ping and any text like `ocean ▸` with the circular Ocean mark in motion. - The ideal motion is fluid current inside the logo: wave bands subtly shear, drift, and churn under the circular clip while the rim stays calm. It should read like ocean current moving inside the mark, not a spinning loader, not a bouncing dot, and not decorative page-load choreography. - Drive it from the existing send-to-first-token pending hook and streaming state in `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/transcript.rs`; do not add daemon state for this. The spinner is surface presentation only. - Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, render the static circular mark with a small live-state glow and no current animation. Idle desktop geometry is 8px dock padding, a 32px minimum writing row, 4px row gap, and 34px toolbar controls (86px total before external margins). No — live recording convention is red, but our live accent is the brand: use `--accent` pulsing dot for "live", `--ok` for connected, `--warn` for reconnecting, `--err` for failed/barge. - Extension side panel (`compact.css`): same system, tighter paddings; never fork colors. ## 7.
