content.text: # Ocean Web Surface — Design System Authority for all visual work in the Leptos web surface (`crates/ocean-surface-ui`, `styles/*.css`, `index.html`). Ocean's OWN identity — not an agency re-brand — applied at **product register**: the UI serves the task; brand energy is rationed, never decorative. Register rule: a user fluent in Linear/Figma/Raycast should trust every control on sight. Familiar affordances, one component vocabulary, restrained color. **Control density is a design defect.** The surface holds exactly the controls the current moment needs; everything else is conditional, collapsed behind one overflow, or revealed on intent (hover/focus). A row of same-weight buttons is failure — one primary affordance, quiet metadata, ghost triggers. ## 1. Identity The OCEAN depth ramp comes from the ASCII splash banner in the TUI (`ocean-os/crates/ocean-tui/src/splash.rs`), deep indigo rising to bright aqua (xterm 17→19→25→31→38→44→50→87). The active logo direction is now the circular neumorphic wave mark, not the ASCII banner and not a terminal prompt glyph. Reference asset: `public/brand/master-1024.png` (mirrored as `public/brand/ocean-mark.svg`). Logo implementation target: - Replace the current three-line `WaveLogo` and text-only header wordmark with an inline SVG circular mark component that preserves the reference geometry: circular badge, stacked wave cutouts, teal-to-blue depth ramp, matte dark relief, and shallow inner/outer shadow. - Keep the SVG inline in the Leptos bundle, not as ``, so the same asset can animate in web and Tauri. Name internal layers (`rim`, `wave-1`, `wave-2`, `wave-3`, `deep-water`, `wordmark`) so CSS can target state motion. - Test three lockups before choosing: mark-only, lowercase `ocean`, and tighter uppercase `OCEAN` with less spacing than the current landing wordmark. - Avoid prompt/code symbolism completely: no `>`, `_`, cursor, brackets, terminal glyphs, sparkle/star motifs, mascots, or Codex-adjacent shapes. - Tauri consumes the same Trunk-built Leptos bundle, so the web logo component is the primary fix for both browser and native shell. Generate Tauri app icons from the final mark only after the web lockup is accepted. Never gradient-clip text. The ramp is always painted as solid colors on discrete elements, or as vector fills inside the circular mark. The page is near-black; the working accent (`--ocean-6` cyan) appears ONLY at: - Primary actions (send, approve, join, submit, create) — solid cyan fill with dark ink (`--fg-on-accent`), never white text, never a gradient fill. - Live/active states: voice orb recording, speaking ring, live dots, active selection fills. - Focus rings (single cyan ring). Everything else is neutral: near-black surfaces, low-opacity white borders, the near-white/grey text ramp. No teal-mint (legacy #7fe7c8), no navy chrome, no magenta/purple (rejected 2026-07-04). ## 2. Tokens (`styles/tokens.css` — the only place colors are defined) Surfaces - `--bg: #060606` page - `--bg-raised: #0A0A0A` bars, panels, drawers - `--bg-elevated: #141414` cards, inputs, chips, wells - `--bg-hover: #1B1C21` hover fill on elevated surfaces - `--bg-well: #23252B` special data wells (code, diff, transcript wells) Text - `--fg: #FAFCFF` headings, primary content - `--fg-2: #B8B9BB` body secondary - `--fg-3: #909098` labels, metadata - `--fg-4: #5A5C63` disabled only — never for readable content Brand — the OCEAN ramp - `--ocean-1..8`: `#00005F #0000AF #005FAF #0087AF #00AFD7 #00D7D7 #00FFD7 #5FFFFF` (identity surfaces only: banner rows, wordmark letters, data-fill gradient) - `--accent: var(--ocean-6)` interactive accent (links, active text, hot states) - `--accent-bright: var(--ocean-7)` live highlights - `--accent-deep: var(--ocean-4)` depth end of data gradients - `--fg-on-accent: #03181A` ink on accent fills — accent fills NEVER take white text - `--gradient: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--ocean-6), var(--ocean-4))` DATA fills (chart bars) only — never buttons, never text - `--accent-soft: rgba(0,215,215,0.12)` tinted fills - `--accent-ring: rgba(0,215,215,0.45)` focus ring color Status (semantic; used for tool state, call state, deltas, diffs) - `--ok: #1ED760`, `--ok-soft: rgba(30, 215, 96, 0.12)` - `--err: #FF4D67`, `--err-soft: rgba(255, 77, 103, 0.12)` - `--warn: #FFB224`, `--warn-soft: rgba(255, 178, 36, 0.12)` - `--info: #6AA6FF`, `--info-soft: rgba(106, 166, 255, 0.12)` - `--running: var(--warn)` (in-flight tool state) Borders - `--border-subtle: rgba(255,255,255,0.06)` - `--border: rgba(255,255,255,0.10)` - `--border-strong: rgba(255,255,255,0.20)` Type - `--font: 'Poppins', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif` - `--mono: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace` - Scale (fixed px, product register): 11 label / 12 small / 13 secondary / 14 body / 15 emphasized / 18 title / 22 display. Body line-height 1.55. - Uppercase labels: 11px, weight 600, `letter-spacing: 0.08em`, `--fg-3`. - Mono is for DATA (paths, ids, tokens, numbers, code), never for UI labels. Radii — pill is GEOMETRY, never chrome - `--radius-sm: 4px` chips, badges, tabs, menu items, mono data chips - `--radius: 6px` inputs, buttons, selects, list rows, dropdown menus - `--radius-lg: 10px` cards, panels, modals, composer dock - `--radius-pill: 999px` true circles/capsules ONLY: status dots, the voice orb, progress bars, scrollbar thumbs.    703	/// surfaces at `cargo test` rather than as a silent runtime drop.

   740	            | AgentEvent::AssistantTextDelta { session_id, .. }
   741	            | AgentEvent::ThinkingDelta { session_id, .. }
   742	            | AgentEvent::ToolCallStarted { session_id, .. }
   743	            | AgentEvent::ToolCallChunk { session_id, .. }
   744	            | AgentEvent::ToolCallFinished { session_id, .. }
   745	            | AgentEvent::TurnFinished { session_id, .. }

# Code Context

## Files Retrieved
1. `docs/OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (full file) - V1 boundaries, Island state/DOM/keyboard contract, and the proposed daemon-owned `WorkAttentionItem` follow-up.
2. `docs/OCEAN_DYNAMIC_ISLAND_BUILD_PLAN.md` (full file) - sequencing; Step 7 explicitly requires daemon truth before richer attention states.
3. `docs/OCEAN_WEB_SURFACE_DESIGN.md` (full file) - token, material, control-density, motion, focus, and status semantics.
4. `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs` (lines 13-203, 230-583, 585-795) - current session model/search, overlay component, accessibility behavior, and unit tests.
5. `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/app.rs` (lines 230-270, 337-362, 461-469, 709-718, 774-825, 1031-1044, 1294-1299) - available daemon signals, Island ownership/mount, overlay arbitration, shortcuts, badge, and existing permission prompt mount.
6. `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/daemon.rs` (lines 540-813, 1220-1305, 1401-1421, 1705-1745, 1933-2004) - focused-session event/control streams, `PendingPermission`, `Daemon` signals, and session summary limitations.
7. `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/components.rs` (lines 1524-1588) - existing mutating permission-card UI that must not be copied into this read-only slice.
8. `styles/island.css` (lines 1-300) - current chip/popover geometry, z-order, focus styles, result rows, and responsive rules.
9. `index.html` (lines 37-41) - Island stylesheet is already wired after chrome.

## Key Code

### Exact frontend signals already available
`Daemon` exposes focused-session-only live state (`daemon.rs:1223-1305`):

```rust
pub streaming: RwSignal<bool>;
pub session_id: RwSignal<Option<String>>;
pub status: RwSignal<String>;
pub session_title: RwSignal<String>;
pub session_list: RwSignal<Vec<SessionSummary>>;
pub active_turn_id: RwSignal<Option<String>>;
pub browser_active: RwSignal<bool>;
pub browser_last_action: RwSignal<Option<String>>;
pub pending_permissions: RwSignal<Vec<PendingPermission>>;
```

The only currently truthful human-attention payload is (`daemon.rs:767-784`):

```rust
pub struct PendingPermission {
    pub permission_id: String,
    pub session_id: String,
    pub tool: String,
    pub reason: String,
    pub args_summary: String,
    pub deciding: bool,
}
```

It is daemon-backed through `/v1/events`, but the client explicitly filters that global control stream to the **focused** session (`daemon.rs:1933-1996`). The agent SSE is likewise replaced on focus changes (`daemon.rs:1705-1734`). `SessionSummary` contains only id/title/root/project/branch/turn count/update time (`daemon.rs:1401-1421`); it has no running, needs-human, failed, or completion state.

The current Island already owns modal focus restoration, query/selection, combobox/listbox semantics, Escape/Tab/arrows, and session switching (`island.rs:285-402, 436-580`). `app.rs` owns mode and mutual exclusion (`app.rs:337-362`) and already mirrors `pending_permissions.len()` to the dock badge (`app.rs:709-718`).

## Architecture

### What can be implemented honestly now
A smallest safe read-only attention popdown can display **pending permission attention for the currently focused session only**. It may show a compact warning/count in the Island chip and a read-only expanded card containing tool, reason, and safely bounded args summary. It must say “permission required” or “needs your attention,” not imply background/global coverage. Keep the existing composer-adjacent `PermissionPrompts` as the sole Approve/Deny surface (`components.rs:1524-1588`). No call to `decide_permission`, no reply composer, no new daemon authority.

A useful pure seam in `island.rs` would be an `IslandAttentionItem` (or extend `IslandResult` with an attention variant) derived from `pending_permissions`, with a stable key (`permission_id`) and explicit `session_id`. Do not overload timestamp-derived `IslandPriority`: it means focused/recent/background, not urgency.

### Missing contracts (block true cross-session Phase 2)
The proposed `WorkAttentionItem` snapshot/stream in both Island docs does not exist. Missing daemon-owned fields/endpoints are: stable item id, kind, optional session id, title/detail, authoritative state (`Idle|Running|NeedsHuman|Failed|Complete`), updated time, priority, initial snapshot/replay, and lifecycle/removal semantics. Also missing:

- Cross-session permission observation: current `/v1/events` subscriber drops non-focused sessions.
- Cross-session run/failure/completion truth: session catalogue timestamps cannot provide it.
- Session/project display metadata on attention items, or a guaranteed join against `session_list`.
- Ordering/deduplication/reconnect contract and event-name subscription contract (named SSE events are silently dropped unless subscribed; `daemon.rs:687-714`).
- Read/acknowledged semantics, if a card can be dismissed.

Do not create a Tauri-local attention store or open one SSE pair per background session; browser connection limits are already documented (`daemon.rs:35-40`). The daemon should supply one snapshot plus one aggregate stream, ideally shared-core HTTP/SSE rather than a Tauri command.

### Smallest safe vertical slice
1. In `island.rs`, derive a read-only focused permission attention view from `daemon.pending_permissions`; add pure tests for empty, ordered/deduped display, session mismatch filtering, and safe empty reason/args rendering.
2. Preserve `IslandMode::{Closed,Browse,Search}`. Render the attention card at the top of the existing popover (before session search/results), only when pending data exists. Do not introduce another overlay.
3. Chip: change dot/count/accessible label conditionally when pending count > 0; no animation. Use `--warn`/`--warn-soft`, not accent (design doc permission-wait semantics).
4. Card: read-only `role="status"` or labelled region with heading “Permission required,” tool, concise reason, optional truncated/pre-wrapped args, and guidance such as “Review in the session below.” It must contain no Approve, Deny, reply input, or dismiss action.
5. Keep click/`Cmd+P` behavior, session rows, `switch_session`, `PermissionPrompts`, dock badge, and web/extension gating unchanged. If the card is only focused-session data, clicking it need not mutate or navigate.
6. Add selectors only to `styles/island.css`; colors remain token-only. Reuse the single elevated popover and plain-row vocabulary—no nested elevated card, pill text control, decorative pulse, or new stylesheet.
7. Validate with one pending permission arriving/removing via daemon SSE, zero/multiple permissions, keyboard-only use, screen reader announcement, narrow/wide Tauri, and no web/extension visual change.

### Accessibility/state requirements
- Keep one modal dialog and current focus capture/restore; do not create a nested dialog.
- Update chip `aria-label` with exact pending count and `aria-expanded`; avoid relying on color/dot alone.
- Permission arrival while closed should be announced by a restrained `aria-live="polite"` status; avoid repeatedly announcing on unrelated reactive updates.
- Expanded card must have a programmatic heading/label; tool/args should remain readable, wrap safely, and not expose raw unbounded payload in compact chrome.
- Escape closes exactly one surface; IME guards remain; focus returns to prior connected element/chip.
- If attention is inserted ahead of listbox results, it is not a listbox `option` and must not disturb `aria-activedescendant`, selected index, Arrow/Enter behavior, or result IDs.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; this slice needs no new motion.
- State clears reactively when `permission_decision` arrives. Do not add local dismiss/read state.

### Likely change locations for the implementation worker
- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs`: attention projection, conditional chip/card markup, tests.
- `styles/island.css`: warning state and read-only card/row styles.
- Possibly `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/daemon.rs`: **only** if introducing a proper aggregate attention wire contract later; not needed for the focused-permission slice.
- `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/app.rs`: likely no change because `Daemon` is already passed to `Island`; touch only if product chooses a new mode/entry policy.
- Do not modify `components.rs` approval actions or stylesheet wiring for this slice.

## Start Here
Open `crates/ocean-surface-ui/src/island.rs` at lines 230-583. It already has the daemon instance, chip, modal state/focus behavior, and the exact popover insertion point; the focused permission signal can be projected there without widening app-level state.

## Residual risks / review questions
- The phrase “daemon-backed attention” may be interpreted as cross-session attention. Current Surface cannot truthfully deliver that; approve the focused-session-only wording or wait for the daemon aggregate contract.
- `/v1/events` is live-tail only in this path; no permission snapshot/replay is evident, so a permission emitted while disconnected may not appear until another recovery mechanism exists.
- `args_summary` may contain sensitive or very large content; compact display needs truncation and the product should decide whether args are shown at all.
- Existing worktree is heavily dirty with the uncommitted V1 Island and unrelated changes; implementation must isolate hunks and avoid reverting them.
